sources.title: Saved vCenter and ESXi connections. Their passwords stay in the cluster and are never shown again.
sources.heading: Connected vCenter & ESXi

source.description: The cluster stores the connection and checks the server's certificate fingerprint before it sends the password.
source.hostHint: vCenter or ESXi host name or IP address
source.passwordKeep: Leave empty to keep the saved password (only if host, port and user stay the same).
source.datacenterHint: If vCenter has several datacenters, write the one to use. ESXi hosts use ha-datacenter; you can leave it empty.
source.vddkHint: Needed for vSAN and vVols. The operator installs nbdkit and VDDK on the nodes.
source.libdirHint: The directory on the nodes where VDDK is unpacked. Empty uses the node setting [vmware] vddk_libdir.
source.untrusted: {{host}} presented a certificate this cluster has not seen. Compare the fingerprint with the one in vCenter before you trust it.
source.deleteDescription: Migrations that use this source must be deleted first. Nothing changes on the VMware side.

errors.name: Use lowercase letters, digits and hyphens (up to 63).
errors.nameTaken: A source with this name already exists.
errors.passwordAgain: Enter the password again when you change the host, port or user.

mode.warmHint: The source keeps running. Changed blocks are copied again and again; downtime is only the cutover.
mode.coldHint: Powered-off VMs are copied once. Running VMs are refused.

migration.cancelDescription: Our snapshots and target volumes are removed. Source VMs stay as they are. VMs already cut over (or cutting over) stay; finalize or revert them afterwards.
migration.cutOverLeft_one: {{count}} VM is cut over but not finished. Finalize or revert it before you delete this migration.
migration.cutOverLeft_other: {{count}} VMs are cut over but not finished. Finalize or revert them before you delete this migration.
migration.deleteDescription: The plan and its items are deleted. Created VMs, volumes and the source VMs stay.

drawer.rollbackFailed: The automatic rollback failed. Do these steps by hand, or retry the rollback:

cutover.description: Each source VM is shut down, the last changes are copied and the new VM is created. If a step fails, the source is powered on again.
cutover.total: About {{time}} of downtime in total (one after another at most).

shutdown.guest: The guest is shut down through VMware Tools (waits up to {{timeout}} s).
shutdown.power-off: The source is powered off without a guest shutdown.

cutover.protect: Source NICs stay disconnected at power-on so the same MAC and IP never come up twice.
cutover.rollback: The source VM is never deleted.

revert.title: Revert {{name}}?
revert.description: {{name}} is stopped and the source VM {{source}} is powered on again.
revert.dataLost: Data written on the new VM since the cutover is not copied back.
revert.keeps: The new VM and its volumes stay, powered off.

finalize.title: Finalize {{name}}?
finalize.description: Our snapshots and change tracking are removed from the source. After this the VM cannot be reverted.

cancelItems.description: Our snapshot and the target volumes are removed. The source VM stays as it is.

wizard.title: New VMware migration
wizard.hint: Go in order: ① connection and mode ② choose VMs ③ map networks and storage ④ limits and cutover ⑤ check each VM. It stays a draft until you start it.
wizard.draftLocked: Draft {{name}} is already saved; its name, source and mode stay.
wizard.vanished_one: {{count}} chosen VM is no longer in the inventory and was unselected.
wizard.vanished_other: {{count}} chosen VMs are no longer in the inventory and were unselected.
wizard.blockedLeftOut_one: {{count}} blocked VM is left out of the migration when it starts.
wizard.blockedLeftOut_other: {{count}} blocked VMs are left out of the migration when it starts.

errors.name: Use lowercase letters, digits and hyphens (up to 63).
errors.nameTaken: A migration with this name already exists.
errors.tooMany: A migration holds up to 200 VMs. Split it into waves.
errors.pool: Choose a pool or a default pool.
errors.range: Enter a whole number in range.

picker.searchHint: Name, path, OS, host or IP

mapping.networksHint: Only networks the chosen VMs use. Leave one unmapped and the check will tell you.
mapping.flat: Put all VMs in one folder
mapping.keepMacsHint: DHCP reservations and licenses bound to a MAC keep working.
mapping.reserveIpsHint: On SDN networks, IPs reported by VMware Tools are reserved for the new VM.
mapping.startAfter: Start the new VM after cutover

policy.maxParallelHint: VMs copied or cut over at the same time in this migration (1–64). More is faster but loads the source and network more.
policy.maxPerHostHint: VMs read at once from one ESXi host (1–64). Fewer means less load on the source host.
policy.maxPerNodeHint: VMs one Orbivisor node receives at once (1–64).
policy.bandwidthHint: The most bandwidth copying may use. Set it to protect the network during business hours. Empty means no limit.
policy.intervalHint: How often changed blocks are copied again (5–1440 minutes). Shorter means less to copy at cutover.
policy.stopAfterHint: Syncing stops if there is no cutover after this long, so our snapshot does not stay on the source. 0 never stops.
policy.shutdownTimeoutHint: The longest wait when shutting the guest down through VMware Tools (30–3600 s).
policy.maxFinalDeltaHint: If the last changes are larger, cutover stops before the source is touched. Empty means no limit.
policy.cutoverAtHint: Cut over automatically at this time. Empty means you cut over by hand once ready.
policy.protectSourceHint: Source NICs are set to stay disconnected at power-on and a note is added.

errors.vmware_vm_not_found: A chosen VM is no longer in the inventory. Read the inventory again.
errors.vm_in_migration: A chosen VM is already in another migration: {{message}}
errors.migration_running: Pause the migration before changing it.
errors.migration_state: The migration cannot do that now: {{message}}
errors.migration_active: Some VMs are not finished. Finalize or revert cut-over VMs and cancel the others, then delete the migration.
errors.password_required: Enter the password again when you change the host, port or user.
errors.migration_busy: Another change is running. Try again.
errors.vm_started: A started VM cannot be removed; cancel it instead.
errors.vmware_vm_state: This VM cannot do that now: {{message}}
errors.not_ready: Only ready, syncing or rolled-back VMs can be cut over.
errors.vmware_permission: The VMware user may not do this: {{message}}
errors.vmware_restricted: This ESXi host is read only (free license). Use a cold migration.
errors.preflight_blocked: The source VM cannot be cut over now:

help.sourcesIntro: To move VMs from VMware, first connect vCenter or ESXi here. VMware migration can then list its VMs for you to pick.
help.sourcesEmpty: Save a vCenter or ESXi address and account once, and VMware migration can pick and move its VMs.
help.migrationsIntro: Move many VMware VMs as one plan. A warm migration copies VMs while they run and powers them off only briefly at cutover.
help.migrationsEmpty: Pick VMs from a connected vCenter or ESXi and map networks and storage once to move many together.
help.name: The name of this connection (e.g. vcenter-seoul). Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens (not at the start or end); it cannot be changed later.
help.user: The VMware user to log in as (e.g. administrator@vsphere.local). It needs permission to read VMs, create and remove snapshots, change settings (CBT on and off, NIC connection, notes), shut down guests and power VMs off and on.
help.password: That user's password. It stays in the cluster and is never shown again.
help.planName: The name of this migration (e.g. wave-1). Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens (not at the start or end).
help.source: The vCenter or ESXi connection to read VMs from. If there is none, add one under Connected vCenter & ESXi first.
help.defaultPool: The pool for disks on datastores set to 'Default pool' above. A shared pool lets VMs move between nodes easily.
help.folderKind: Put the moved VMs together in one folder, or rebuild VMware's folder tree.
help.folder: The Orbivisor folder for the moved VMs (or the VMware folder tree). They inherit its permissions.
help.node: The node the new VMs are created on. Automatic picks a node with room.
help.driverIso: A virtio driver ISO to put in Windows VMs, for switching to the fast virtual devices after the move.
help.devices: Choose disk and network card types automatically by guest OS, or the same for every VM.
help.diskBus: This applies to every VM moved. virtio-blk: the fast virtual device — only if every VM has the driver (install it on Windows first, or it does not boot). SATA: a compatible device Windows sees without drivers.
help.nicModel: This applies to every VM moved. virtio: the fast virtual device — only if every VM has the driver (install it on Windows first). e1000e: a compatible device that works without drivers.
help.shutdown: How the source is turned off at cutover. Guest shutdown (recommended) lets the OS shut itself down; power off cuts it at once.
help.startAfter: When on, the new VM starts as soon as cutover finishes. Off leaves it stopped so you can check it first.
